title: Preparedness for the households that standard advice forgets
h1: Preparedness for renters, apartments, tight budgets, elder care and disability access
dek: Standard advice quietly assumes a house, a car, storage space, spare money and a body that can use the stairs. Here is what the official sources say for the households that do not fit, where they run out, and who to ask.
description: Preparedness for renters, apartment dwellers, tight budgets, older adults, caregivers and people with disabilities, using FEMA, CDC, ACL, USFA and Red Cross sources.
recheck: If Ready.gov, FEMA, the CDC, ACL or HUD revise the pages cited, or at the next quarterly source sweep.

source_use.start-usfa-high-rise: Know your exits, practice your route, keep stair doors closed, do not use elevators in a fire, call 911 and shelter in place or wait on a clear landing if you cannot use the stairs (fire only), not all tall buildings meet modern standards.
source_use.start-hud-multifamily-template: That HUD Exchange hosts an optional planning template for multifamily owners, with its own disclaimer, and lists resident handouts and an evacuation special-assistance form in its table of contents. Only 12 of 79 pages were read; no legal or program requirement is claimed.
source_use.start-ready-financial: Renters insurance, flood coverage caveat, small cash, document storage, benefits by direct deposit, ID for FEMA assistance, scam cautions.
source_use.start-fema-housing: Help after a declared disaster: rent, lodging reimbursement, serious needs; the eligibility conditions as printed on 2026-10-30; may qualify even with insurance; how to apply; not a reimbursement for lost power or food.
source_use.ready-are-you-ready: Insurance for an apartment, lease documents, emergency savings, cash, 72-hour framing.
source_use.start-ready-power: Outage effects, medical devices, refrigeration times, generator and stove cautions.
source_use.start-ready-disability: Support network, key, registries, dialysis, power priority list, assistive devices, heat risk, kit tips.
source_use.start-ready-older-adults: Take Control in 1, 2, 3; support-network key; clinics' emergency plans; transport; insurance card copies.
source_use.start-redcross-older-adults: Plan to stay two weeks or evacuate, 30 days of medication, two ways out of every room, registries, renter's insurance, review every six months.
source_use.start-acl-emergency: Chronic conditions among older adults, support network, Medical Information Card, Eldercare Locator, DIAL, Disaster Distress Helpline, emPOWER, service-provider obligations.
source_use.start-cdc-disability-plan: Contact list and check-ins, alerts, evacuation options, practice and annual review.
source_use.start-cdc-disability-evacuate: Accessible transport may not be available; ADA shelters; service and emotional support animals.
source_use.start-cdc-pyh-prescriptions: Emergency supply of medicines, medicine list, state refill laws.
source_use.start-ready-alerts: Alert systems and the limits of each.
